title: Differentiable Net-Moving and Local Congestion Mitigation for Routability-Driven Global Placement
problem: Cell inflation for local congestion mitigation can over-inflate or move cells back into congested areas; global net bounding box minimization may include irrelevant congestion or miss actual bottlenecks; unbalanced placement density degrades pin accessibility.
motivation: Routing congestion is a critical bottleneck in modern VLSI physical design; better congestion mitigation during global placement can avoid expensive physical routing failures.
method: The approach tracks cell inflation over time using momentum-based ratios to prevent over-inflation in local congestion areas. It models global congestion through Poisson's equation (a physics equation describing how quantities spread through space), making this model differentiable for gradient-based optimization to guide net placement. Virtual cells guide each two-pin net placement, while cell density around power and ground rails adjusts based on congestion patterns.
key_novelty: It uses Poisson's equation to create a differentiable model of global congestion, enabling gradient-based optimization for net placement with virtual cell guidance.
contributions: Momentum-based cell inflation considering historical ratios for improved local congestion mitigation
Differentiable Poisson-derived congestion function with virtual cell guidance for net movements
Placement density adjustment around power/ground rails based on routing congestion
40% average DRV reduction on ISPD 2015 benchmarks with comparable wirelength and via count

metrics.other: 40% DRV reduction; comparable wirelength and via count

baselines: Leading routability-driven placers on ISPD 2015 contest benchmarks
limitations: Limited to 2D placement; 3D placement extensions not discussed; scalability to 10M+ cell designs not validated.
primary_theme: Differentiable Poisson-based congestion minimization in routability-driven global placement
